chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man for whom the daytime prayers were missed, when should he make them up? He (peace be upon him) said: Whenever he wishes. If he wishes, after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after Isha.

key_terms.يَقْضِيهَا: He makes them up / fulfills the obligation

ai.seo_question: When can missed daytime prayers be made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in compensating for missed daytime prayers, affirming that the obligation can be fulfilled at any time after the specific prayer window closes, such as after Maghrib or Isha. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the *qada* of obligatory prayers is not bound by the strict temporal constraints of their original performance, offering practical ease for believers who miss prayers due to sleep or forgetfulness. The narration highlights the balance between maintaining ritual continuity and accommodating human limitations within the Shia legal tradition.
